candidates.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
candidates.content: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. candidates.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
candidates.content: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63times speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achi

candidates.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
candidates.content: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. candidates.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
candidates.content: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...] Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. — Levent Alpöge , alpo.ge/remark.pdf Tags: anthropic , claude , generative-ai , mathematics , ai , llms , levent-alpoge

candidates.title: llm 0.37.3
candidates.content: Release: llm 0.37.3 A bug fix release for LLM , mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software. Homebrew now ships the latest SQLite, 3.54.1 , which includes a fix that broke LLM's logging code . Short version: in SQLite 3.54.0 the following SQL: select json_object('a', (select json_array(1))) Returns this: {"a":[1]} But in 3.54.1 the same query returns this: {"a":"[1]"} According to D. Richard Hipp : That was a bug fix. Per the documentation, (SELECT json_array(...)) returns SQL text, not JSON. Hence the 3.54.1 behavior is correct and 3.54.0 was a bug. The workaround looks like this: select json_object('a', json((select json_array(1)))) Tags: llm , webassembly , sqlite , generative-ai , ai , llms , d-richard-hipp

candidates.title: A Vaccine (STEMVAC) for Improving Survival in Patients With Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Moderate or Extensive Residual Cancer Burden
candidates.content: [PHASE2] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: University of Washington | 适应症: Anatomic Stage I Breast Cancer AJCC v8, Anatomic Stage II Breast Cancer AJCC v8, Anatomic Stage III Breast Cancer AJCC v8, Triple-Negative Breast Carcinoma. This phase II trial evaluates whether a multi-antigen vaccine called STEMVAC improves disease-free survival after surgery in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and moderate or extensive residual cancer burden. TNBC has an aggressive clinical course and poorer disease-free survival compared to other subtypes. While patients who have no remaining tumor in the breast or lymph nodes after surgery have excellent long-term outcomes, patients with moderate or extensive residual cancer burden remain at high risk for early disease return and poorer prognosis. STEMVAC is designed to target proteins that tumor cells use when they become more aggressive and start to spread, and it is believed to work by boosting the immune system to recognize and destroy the invader tumor cells that are causing the disease. Giving STEMVAC after surgery may improve disease-free survival rates in TNBC patients with moderate or extensive residual cancer burden.

candidates.title: Illicit Injectable Peptides—Reply
candidates.content: In Reply We thank Dr Janovsky for highlighting the emergence of illicit peptide markets in Brazil and for extending the discussion beyond the jurisdictions considered in our original Viewpoint. Janovsky’s observations reinforce our central argument that the rapid expansion of unapproved peptide use is no longer a country-specific regulatory issue, but an increasingly global public health challenge. The Brazilian experience is striking because it mirrors patterns emerging elsewhere. Illicit peptides are increasingly marketed online using remarkably consistent narratives centered on recovery, muscle growth, healthy aging, and health optimization, despite limited human evidence supporting these claims. As Janovsky notes, concerns extend beyond efficacy to product quality, manufacturing standards, and unsupported therapeutic claims.

candidates.title: Trials of Treatment Deescalation, Deimplementation, and Discontinuation—Reply
candidates.content: In Reply Drs Mathioudakis and Chatzimavridou-Grigoriadou raise an excellent point in response to our JAMA+ Trials themed Editorial on deescalation, discontinuation, and deimplementation trials: often, the effects of discontinuing a health intervention extend beyond the simple absence of benefit (or harm) from continued intervention use. Instead, the act or process of discontinuation itself can have direct, important, and potentially time-dependent effects on outcomes—for example, through withdrawal or rebound effects that can manifest after intervention discontinuation and may or may not subside over time.

candidates.title: [Perspectives] What do artists know?
candidates.content: Until the day my newborn son died, I worked as an artist. I spent each day in the studio making drawings and films, over 15 years preparing work for exhibitions, commissions, and eventually a doctorate in fine art. After he died (in my arms, peacefully, not unexpectedly), I directed everything I had learned as an artist into writing the story of his birth and death. As it turned out, over those years in the studio I had developed aptitudes well matched to drawing meaning from experience too adverse to bear.

candidates.title: NF-kappaB dimer exchange on the promoter facilitates transcription activation of NF-kappaB repressed IRF3 target genes—a plausible mechanism
candidates.content: Abstract The NF-κB and the IRF family of transcription factors are the key regulators of innate immune response in vertebrates. Depending upon the state of the cell the NF-κB subunits can activate as well as repress transcription of many genes by binding to its cognate κB sequence on the promoter/enhancers of various genes. The NF-κB proteins function as dimers, and variation in dimer composition represents one of the mechanisms for regulating transcription of specific genes. The homodimer of p50 NF-κB subunit is known to maintain a subset of IRF3 target genes under repressed state by binding to the promoter site called the G-IRE. G-IRE is an incomplete κB sequence juxtaposed with the IRF3 cognate IRE. Our in vitro results show that the NF-κB p50 homodimer can readily exchange on the κB DNA to form the NF-κB p50-RelA heterodimer. This dimer exchange on the DNA facilitates the binding of DNA binding domain of IRF3 to the G-IRE site required for transcription activation of these IRF3 target genes.

candidates.content: arXiv:2611.25342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated ICAO/ISO face-image compliance analysers provide criterion-level pass/fail decisions, yet these verdicts do not quantify uncertainty when deciding whether to accept, reject, or retake a photograph. We investigate conformal prediction as a triage layer for BioGaze, evaluating 14 compliance criteria on the synthetic TONO benchmark. Without retraining the analyser, we fit per-criterion logistic classifiers and compare marginal and label-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction with conventional abstention rules using subject-disjoint splits. Marginal conformal prediction achieved approximately 0.90 overall coverage but substantially under-covered violations, with a ten-partition mean of 0.37 for one criterion. The corresponding Mondrian means ranged from 0.89 to 0.92 across criteria. However, most of the reduction in criterion-level false positives came from the logistic layer (0.145 to 0.048), while tuned abstention rules achieved lower false-positive rates than Mondrian at comparable retake rates. candidates.title: Measurable Does Not Imply Transportable: A Prospective Audit of Model Explanations in Multi-Year Field Trials
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.25692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model explanations are increasingly used as scientific evidence, yet it remains unclear what they license scientists to conclude beyond the data on which they were constructed. When a fine-grained explanation fails to replicate, the failure may be attributed to noisy measurement of its target, raising a fundamental question: does reliable measurement imply a reproducible explanation? We test this directly. We formalize prospective explanation transportability: the extent to which an explanation learned from past data is recovered in a genuinely future context. This property is distinct from feature importance and measurement reliability. Using multi-year Genomes-to-Fields maize trials, where each new year is a real future context rather than a random resample, we evaluate 16 agronomically interpretable environmental concepts across five forward splits and one prospectively locked test year. Coarse environment-level explanations transport reliably (median cosine 0.83); their locked 2024 value, 0.811, fell within a prespecified 80% bootstrap percentile interval. candidates.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.26598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable

candidates.title: Antom 3-in-1 Transformer: A Payment Foundation Model
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.25403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the development of Antom 3-in-1 Transformer, a payment foundation model that integrates sequence, tabular, and graph representations for payment risk detection. The model contains approximately 7B parameters, with approximately 1.7B activated per task route. Antom 3-in-1 Transformer is pretrained to learn reusable behavioral and relational representations, primarily on Ant International's internal payment data. In a cross-business transfer experiment, pretraining improves the target business metric by 34.5% over the same architecture trained from scratch. With only 25% of the training labels, the pretrained model outperforms the full-label scratch baseline in Average Precision (AP) and Recall@0.5% on different merchant domains. In a four-month online experiment on Ant International's billion-scale payment platform, the model reduced the overall loss rate by 37.88% relative to XGB-Online.

candidates.title: Mitek Systems appoints Laura Apel as chief marketing officer
candidates.content: Mitek Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: MITK), a global leader in digital identity verification and fraud prevention, today announced the appointment of Laura Apel as Chief Marketing Officer, effective November 16, 2026. Reporting directly to Chief Executive Officer Edward H. West, Apel will lead Mitek's global marketing organization, overseeing brand, demand generation, product marketing and communications.

candidates.title: Google Wallet lands on iOS in the US
candidates.content: Today, we’re bringing Google Wallet to iOS users across the U.S., making it faster to get what you need and easier to organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place.

candidates.title: Canadian fintech Float commits $5m to Quebec
candidates.content: Float Financial (Float), the Canadian smart financial management platform, announces a $5 million investment in Quebec, marking its first establishment in the province.

candidates.title: Geordie Shore star sentenced for promoting high-risk investments on social media
candidates.content: A UK reality TV star and a 'finfluencer' have been sentenced and fined for illegally promoting an unauthorised foreign exchange trading scheme on social media.
